title: When Does Frequency Decomposition Benefit Physics-Informed Neural Networks? A Preliminary Ablation Study
abstract: arXiv:2608.24940v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Partial differential equations (PDEs) often have high-frequency and multi-scale features that neural networks struggle to approximate. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) build the governing equations directly into training, but suffer from spectral bias: they learn low-frequency components faster than high-frequency ones. Techniques such as Fourier feature embeddings and sinusoidal activations address this, but most studies assume they help across the board without checking which spectral regimes actually benefit. We introduce a dual-branch, spectrally-gated architecture (DBSG-PINN) that splits low- and high-frequency components into separate subnetworks joined by an adaptive gate, and use it to run a partially controlled ablation of frequency decomposition and spectral routing. translated_title: 频率分解何时有益于物理信息神经网络？一项初步消融研究
translated_abstract: 偏微分方程（PDEs）通常具有高频和多尺度特征，而神经网络难以逼近这些特征。物理信息神经网络（PINNs）将控制方程直接纳入训练过程，但存在谱偏差问题：它们学习低频分量的速度比高频分量更快。诸如傅里叶特征嵌入和正弦激活等技术可以解决这一问题，但大多数研究假设这些技术在所有情况下都有帮助，而未检查哪些谱区域实际上受益。我们引入了一种双分支、谱门控架构（DBSG-PINN），该架构将低频和高频分量分离到由自适应门连接的不同子网络中，并利用它进行频率分解和谱路由的部分控制消融研究。我们在五个一维基准PDE上进行了测试，范围从平滑的单尺度问题到振荡的多尺度问题。频率分解在特定条件下显示出显著收益。
tldr: 本文提出一种双分支谱门控架构（DBSG-PINN），通过消融实验揭示频率分解仅在多尺度或高频主导的PDE问题中显著提升PINN性能，而在平滑单尺度问题上收益有限。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a dual-branch spectrally-gated architecture (DBSG-PINN) and, through ablation studies, reveals that frequency decomposition significantly benefits PINNs only in multi-scale or high-frequency-dominated PDE problems, with limited gains on smooth single-scale ones.
